13 A sign outside a shop is suspended from a rusty horizontal hinge at its top end. The sign hangs in
equilibrium at an angle of 25 to the vertical, as shown.
hinge
25
sign
The sign is a square of side length 52 cm and uniform thickness. It has a mass of 36 kg.
What is the moment of the weight of the sign about the hinge?
A
39 N m
B
78 N m
C
83 N m
D
92 N m

hints: Notice the weight acts vertically down from the centre of the uniform square, $0.26\text{ m}$ along the sign from the hinge.
Moment needs the perpendicular distance from the hinge to the vertical line of the weight, so look at the $25^{\circ}$ triangle between the sign and the vertical.
First calculate $W = mg$ for $36\text{ kg}$, then multiply by $0.26\sin25^{\circ}$ and check the unit is $\text{N m}$.
walkthrough: Weight acts at the centre of mass. For the uniform $52\text{ cm}$ square this is halfway along it, so distance from hinge is $d = 0.52/2 = 0.26\text{ m}$.
Calculate the weight: $W = mg = 36 \times 9.81 = 353.2\text{ N}$ acting vertically downwards.
Moment about hinge is $W$ times perpendicular distance. From the $25^{\circ}$ tilt to the vertical, that distance is $d_{\perp} = d\sin25^{\circ} = 0.26 \times \sin25^{\circ}$.
Rounded to two significant figures this is $39\text{ N m}$. This is option A.

A.explanation: Weight acts at the centre $0.26\text{ m}$ from the hinge with perpendicular distance $0.26\sin25^{\circ}$, giving about $39\text{ N m}$.

B.explanation: About $78\text{ N m}$ is twice too large because it uses the full $0.52\text{ m}$ side length instead of the $0.26\text{ m}$ distance to the centre of mass.

C.explanation: About $83\text{ N m}$ comes from using $\cos25^{\circ}$ instead of $\sin25^{\circ}$ for the perpendicular distance from the vertical weight line.

D.explanation: About $92\text{ N m}$ is $W \times 0.26\text{ m}$ with no angular factor, ignoring that the sign is tilted $25^{\circ}$ from the vertical.
